pathway_name: Citizenship — Holocaust Descendants (§ 58c StbG, BGBl. I 96/2019)
notes: MAJOR pathway added by BGBl. I 96/2019, effective 1 September 2020. By written declaration (Anzeige) under § 58c StbG, descendants in the direct descending line of persons who were citizens or nationals of a successor state of the former Austro-Hungarian monarchy, or stateless, who had their main residence in Austrian territory and fled abroad before 15 May 1955 due to Nazi persecution (NSDAP/Reich authorities) or persecution for their commitment to the democratic Republic of Austria, acquire Austrian citizenship. NO Austrian residence requirement: applicant may live abroad and submit the declaration via the Austrian consular representation (§ 58c Abs 8). NO language requirement (the integration/civics provisions of § 10a do NOT apply — § 58c references only § 10 Abs 1 Z 2-6, 8 and Abs 2 Z 1, 3-7). Procedure is GEBÜHRENFREI per § 58c Abs 9 (declaration, decision, and supporting documents including certificates, civil-status documents and translations). Adoptees (Wahlkinder) adopted as minors count as descendants (§ 58c Abs 6). Dual citizenship is retained as a legal effect: § 58c operates by Anzeige (declaration), not by Verleihung (grant), so the renunciation requirements of § 20 StbG and § 10 Abs 3 StbG (which apply only to Verleihung) do not apply. ~10,000+ applications since entry into force (Ministry of Interior figures, not in statute). Decision is constitutive from the day the declaration reaches the competent authority (§ 58c Abs 7).

A foreigner acquires Austrian citizenship if they have been falsely treated as a citizen by an Austrian authority for at least 15 years uninterrupted, without fault. Being treated as a citizen includes having been issued a citizenship certificate (Staatsbürgerschaftsnachweis), passport, or national ID card. The authority must notify the foreigner of the false treatment in writing and inform them of the 6-month deadline to declare under Abs 2. Acquisition is effective retroactively from the day of first false treatment (§ 57 Abs 1). 6-month declaration deadline is waived if the foreigner has completed Austrian military or civilian service (§ 57 Abs 3). Declaration may be filed via Austrian consular representation abroad (§ 57 Abs 4). Procedure is GEBÜHRENFREI per § 57 Abs 5. NOTE: This row does NOT cover ordinary 'Wiederverleihung' (re-acquisition for former Austrians who lost citizenship by foreign naturalisation) — that pathway is the § 10 Abs 4 Z 1 residence-waiver for foreigners who held Austrian citizenship for ≥10 years uninterrupted and lost it not by withdrawal, which is normally exercised via the general naturalisation pathway (AT-N-001) with the residence requirement waived. § 10 Abs 4 Z 1 is structurally a relaxation of AT-N-001 conditions, not a separate pathway with its own ID.

The reduced-residency provision shortens the ordinary 5-year continuous residence requirement of AZ-N-001 for applicants who can demonstrate Azerbaijani ethnic origin (typically through birth records, family registration in Soviet-era documents, or parent/grandparent's Azerbaijani citizenship).
